## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:


$$
\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i
$$
```{r load-data}
library(ggplot2)
data(mtcars)
```
```{r stats}

summary(mtcars[, c("mpg", "hp", "wt")])

# Calculate correlation between weight and MPG
cor(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)

```
## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r Plot, echo=FALSE}

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = factor(cyl)), size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Vehicle Weight vs. Fuel Efficiency",
    x = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
    y = "Miles per Gallon",
    color = "Cylinders"
  ) 
```

> The visualization confirms the inverse relationship: heavier cars consume more fuel. The color coding by cylinder count also reveals that vehicles with more cylinders tend to be heavier and less efficient.
